rule: Each L-corner object shoots a diagonal ray in the direction it points; when the ray hits another object it reflects (bounces) and continues, keeping its colour, until leaving the grid.
gap: Rays only go in fixed directions and stop/pass; needs diagonal ray direction from shape orientation plus reflection off obstacles (bounce trajectory).

rule: Each coloured bar touching the wall is projected through the wall as a dotted ray whose period equals the bar's length (colour every n cells), the colour nearest the wall winning overlaps.
gap: Ray through wall exists, but the dot period must be computed from the segment's length, with layered per-colour priority.

rule: A coloured bar on one grid edge defines a band; moving away from it, rows (columns) alternate with period 6: even offsets paint the band with the bar colour, odd offsets clear the band to background, and every third even offset recolours all object cells along that whole line to 3.
gap: Field needs an edge-bar marker (not a cell), band-membership and input-colour in the key, and orientation from which edge holds the bar.

rule: Colour-1 cells act like a conserved liquid: the topmost loose 1s are removed and the same number of 1s is poured into the lowest open gaps between the coloured walls (filling bottom-up, inside basins).
gap: Needs a fluid/pouring behaviour with mass conservation: count removed cells and fill basin cells bottom-up; gravity/fill-enclosed don't conserve count.

rule: A small hub object has a differently coloured marker on each side; each scattered shape is moved to dock onto the hub side of its own colour, rotated so it points outward and overlaps the marker, and the rest is cleared.
gap: Needs docking: move each object to the colour-matched side of a hub, rotating it into that side's frame; move-until-contact lacks target selection and rotation.

rule: Same-colour dots are vertices of polygon outlines that get drawn (orthogonal and 45-degree edges); where a dot has an adjacent dot of another colour, a parallel offset copy of that outline is drawn in the second colour.
gap: Connect only joins aligned pairs; needs polygon construction from vertex sets with diagonal edges and an offset (concentric) copy cued by companion dots.

rule: Foreign-colour cells lodged inside a host shape are removed and re-emitted as a straight line of the same number of cells sticking out of the host along its axis/apex (clipped at the border).
gap: Needs 'inside host' relation, counting intruder cells, and a ray of that length from the host's apex direction rather than a fixed-direction ray.

rule: The input's horizontal stripes, read top to bottom, become concentric square rings from outside in; output side is 2*(rows)-2 so the last stripe forms the centre.
gap: Needs a row-to-ring coordinate remap, colours read from the input, and computed output size; field maps codes only to constant colours.

rule: On a noisy periodic background, large coloured frames each contain smaller framed panels holding sparse glyphs; the output is the contents of one target panel derived by analogy between the panel pairs (exact derivation unclear).
gap: Needs hierarchical frame/panel parsing on a noisy periodic background and analogical (A:B::C:?) transfer between panels; panel split assumes separator lines.

rule: Each object contains a marker cell; the object is translated along one axis so that its marker lines up with the same-coloured reference cell on the grid edge (row or column given by the reference's side).
gap: Move only goes until contact; needs translation to achieve alignment of an internal marker with a same-colour edge reference, axis chosen by reference position.

rule: The grid has a template half whose region contains background-coloured holes and a pieces half with multi-colour patches; output is the template half with each hole filled by the patch of matching shape/size.
gap: Same-shape matching exists for recolouring, but needs hole-to-piece matching across halves, copying multi-colour patch contents, and cropping the template half.

rule: Crop the large template block; each hole in it is filled with the colour most frequently used by the scattered small shapes having the same shape as that hole.
gap: Same-shape recolouring exists, but needs holes as shape keys, a majority vote over many same-shape donors with differing colours, and cropping the template.

rule: Small 0-coloured holes inside the 1 regions get a 7 halo on their 8-neighbouring 1 cells, while stray single 1 pixels in the 0 regions are erased; large 0 areas are untouched.
gap: Behavior must treat colour-0 holes as objects and key on a size class, not exact shape, so unseen hole shapes (diagonal chains) generalise.

rule: The grid is a graph of 2x2 node blocks joined by thin edge paths; the route linking the two terminal nodes (the pair of the distinguished colour) is highlighted: its edges turn 5 and its intermediate nodes turn 3.
gap: Needs graph parsing (nodes/edges with diagonal steps) and path search between terminal nodes, then recolouring only route elements; connect handles only aligned pairs.

rule: Small shapes above are removed and stamped at the bottom of the horizontal band whose body colour matches them, keeping their columns, recoloured with that band's palette (matching colour to band edge colour, other colour to band body).
gap: Needs chaining: colour-matched target band selection, drop to band floor, and palette re-mapping from the band's own two colours.

rule: Crop the block of solid colour panels; each panel's count of stray dots matches the hole count of one loose shape, and that shape is placed inside the panel (panel colour as a 1-cell frame).
gap: Needs counting dots per panel and holes per shape, matching by equal count, and pasting shapes into panels; no assembly-by-matching primitive.

rule: The holey container is upscaled x2 (holes become container colour) and each hole, read as a shape at half scale, is filled by the loose shape whose form matches it at x2; singleton noise is ignored.
gap: Needs scale-invariant shape matching between holes and pieces (factor 2) and pasting pieces into the upscaled container; upscale alone cannot place pieces.

rule: Loose small shapes are erased; each hollow rectangle receives, along its middle row from the right, one dot (every other cell) per loose shape of its own colour.
gap: Needs counting same-colour objects and rendering the count as a dotted tally inside the matching frame; no numerosity-to-drawing primitive.

rule: Fill the 0-masked blocks of a symmetric mosaic using its transpose symmetry plus horizontal/vertical mirror symmetry about an off-centre axis (between rows/cols 15 and 16).
gap: Self-model needs mirror axes not centred on the grid (offset 15.5 in a 30-grid) and composing them with transpose to fill regions masked in both.

rule: A free two-colour piece is rotated/flipped and moved so that its protruding part plugs exactly into the notch of a host shape, like a key into a lock; the piece's original position is cleared.
gap: Needs search over D8 poses and placements of a piece to fit a host's concavity; move-until-contact uses a fixed pose and direction.

rule: Output is the interior of the framed window rectangle, showing the parts of other (possibly periodically patterned) rectangle outlines that pass behind it, completed from their visible parts.
gap: Needs amodal completion of occluded rectangle outlines (extents and periodic border colours) under a window, then cropping it; no symmetry to exploit.

rule: The top-left quadrant holds a template (core block with coloured satellites); every other quadrant's core is completed with the template's satellites, mirrored to that quadrant's orientation and scaled to that core's size.
gap: Quadrant mirror symmetry is present but at differing scales; needs template transfer anchored on the core with scale factor inferred from core size.

rule: A seed colour inside an open container floods the container's interior and pours out through its open side, spreading as a widening 45-degree cone until the grid edge; stray noise cells block nothing.
gap: Fill-enclosed needs closure; needs flood from a seed through an opening, then cone-shaped spreading whose direction comes from the container's open side.

rule: From the 3 seed on the border, a 3-coloured path is drawn across the grid, detouring around each wall segment with a one-cell clearance and turning back toward its course; 1s in the walls become 2.
gap: Rays stop or pass obstacles; needs a path-drawing behaviour that wraps around walls with fixed clearance, choosing turn direction, until exiting the grid.

rule: Glyphs in the header are looked up in a fixed glyph catalogue below and each match gets a 3 surround; if the matches form one full catalogue row/column the header and footer turn 3, otherwise the footer turns 2.
gap: Needs query-to-catalogue same-shape-and-colour matching across regions, then a global alignment test on matches selecting the header/footer colouring.

rule: Every 9 that can reach the central 3x3 box without crossing 6 walls is removed (becomes 7) and the box cells are filled with that many 9s in reading order; walled-off 9s stay.
gap: Needs reachability (connectivity through background, blocked by walls), counting reachable cells, and filling a target box with that count in reading order.

rule: A legend of coloured glyphs encodes hole counts (glyph colour <-> number of holes); every grey blob is recoloured with the legend colour whose hole count equals its own, and blobs with no matching count are erased.
gap: Legend binds colour to a hole count, varying per grid; needs reading the in-grid legend and matching objects by hole count, not by shape.

rule: Outside a 5-framed panel, a legend pairs each block colour with a small glyph in another colour; the panel is cropped and each solid block inside is redrawn as its paired glyph pattern in the paired colour.
gap: Legends are 2-cell colour maps; needs a colour-to-glyph-pattern legend (shape plus colour) applied to blocks, combined with cropping the framed panel.

rule: Coloured wires with gaps and marker cells are repaired: 2-marked ends are reconnected (rerouted) and 4-marked cells mark turns/continuations, gaps are bridged, and crossings take the correct over/under colour; exact marker semantics unclear.
gap: Connect joins aligned same-colour cells only; needs marker cells interpreted as wire-routing instructions (reconnect, turn) and crossing layering.
